description: All dashboard pages and the complete analysis experience. This is the core product experience. Depends on all previous FEATs. Creates the dashboard layout, all 10 protected pages (dashboard, resume upload, analyze, analysis detail, skills, resources, roadmap, progress, profile, settings), and wires everything together end-to-end.
steps: Step 1 — Create app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx. Server Component. This layout wraps all dashboard pages. It should: (a) check auth cookie using Next.js 16 async cookies() — const cookieStore = await cookies(); (b) if no valid token, redirect to /login using redirect() from next/navigation; (c) render a flex layout with Sidebar on the left and main content area on the right; (d) include a top Navbar. Import AuthProvider from hooks/useAuth.ts and wrap children so client components can access auth state. Files: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx

Step 2 — Create app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx. Server Component initially fetches no data (uses demo data via client). Client renders: (a) 'Welcome back, [Name]' header with target role; (b) 4 StatsCards row: Overall Score (78/100), ATS Match (72%), Skills Match (68%), Profile Strength (74%) — each with appropriate icon and color; (c) RecentAnalysis component showing DEMO_ANALYSIS; (d) SkillGapCard list for top 3 missing skills (SQL, Power BI, Statistics); (e) RecommendedActions numbered list. This page should be 'use client' since it calls useAuth() to get the user name and fetches analyses from /api/analysis. Files: app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx

Step 3 — Create app/(dashboard)/resume/page.tsx. 'use client'. The resume upload flow. State machine: 'idle' → 'uploading' → 'uploaded' → 'editing'. Renders: (a) in idle/uploading state: ResumeUpload component with drag-drop zone; (b) after upload: ResumePreview showing extracted data, with ResumeEditor for inline editing; (c) 'Continue to Analysis' button at bottom that links to /analyze with the resumeId. If user already has a resume, show it with option to re-upload. Files: app/(dashboard)/resume/page.tsx

Step 4 — Create app/(dashboard)/analyze/page.tsx. 'use client'. Target job selection page. Shows: (a) role selector using Select component with options: Data Analyst, AI/ML Engineer, Software Developer, Web Developer, Data Scientist, Business Analyst, Custom; (b) if Custom selected, show text input for custom role name; (c) large Textarea for job description paste; (d) helper text 'Paste the full job description for the most accurate analysis'; (e) 'Analyze My Resume' button. On submit: call POST /api/analysis, show LoadingState component with step-by-step animation, then redirect to /analysis/[id]. Files: app/(dashboard)/analyze/page.tsx

Step 5 — Create app/(dashboard)/analysis/[id]/page.tsx. 'use client'. The most important page. In Next.js 16, params is a Promise: const { id } = await params — but since this is 'use client', use useParams() hook from next/navigation instead (useParams() is synchronous in client components). Fetches analysis from GET /api/analysis/[id]. Shows LoadingState while fetching. After load, renders 6-tab layout using Tabs component: Tab 1 'Overview': OverallScore component (ScoreRing + 4 dimension bars) + strengths/weaknesses lists; Tab 2 'ATS Report': ATSAnalysis component; Tab 3 'Skill Gaps': SkillGapAnalysis component; Tab 4 'Content': ContentAnalysis component; Tab 5 'Improvements': ImprovementSuggestions component; Tab 6 'Resources': ResourceCard list grouped by skill gap + ProjectRecommendation list. Files: app/(dashboard)/analysis/[id]/page.tsx

Step 6 — Create app/(dashboard)/skills/page.tsx. 'use client'. Skill profile page. Fetches latest analysis. Shows: (a) header with user's target role; (b) overall skill match percentage with ScoreRing; (c) for each skill in the role's required skills, a SkillBar showing present/absent with gap visualization; (d) critical gaps section with SkillGapCard for each critical missing skill, including 'Why it matters', 'What to do', and top 2 resources; (e) 'Start Learning' button linking to /resources. Files: app/(dashboard)/skills/page.tsx

Step 7 — Create app/(dashboard)/resources/page.tsx. 'use client'. Resource library. Fetches latest analysis. Shows: (a) filter bar with skill selector (dropdown), type filter (course/article/video/book), and free/paid toggle; (b) ResourceCard grid filtered by selections; (c) ProjectRecommendation section below. Implements client-side filtering. Files: app/(dashboard)/resources/page.tsx

Step 8 — Create app/(dashboard)/roadmap/page.tsx. 'use client'. Career roadmap visualization. Defines a static 5-stage roadmap based on the user's target role and skill gaps from their latest analysis. Stages: 1) Foundation (fix critical gaps), 2) Skill Building (address high-priority gaps), 3) Projects (build portfolio projects), 4) Resume Update (apply all improvements), 5) Job Applications (submit to target roles). Each stage rendered by RoadmapStep component. Shows estimated total timeline. Files: app/(dashboard)/roadmap/page.tsx

Step 9 — Create app/(dashboard)/progress/page.tsx. 'use client'. Progress tracking. Fetches progress history from GET /api/progress. Shows: (a) ProgressChart (recharts LineChart) with score history; (b) 'improvement from last analysis' delta badge; (c) per-skill progress bars if multiple analyses exist; (d) empty state if only one analysis. Files: app/(dashboard)/progress/page.tsx

Step 10 — Create app/(dashboard)/profile/page.tsx. 'use client'. User profile. Shows/edits: name, email, target role, LinkedIn URL. Uses react-hook-form. Calls PUT /api/profile on save. Shows current analysis summary. Files: app/(dashboard)/profile/page.tsx

Step 11 — Create app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx. 'use client'. Settings page: notification preferences (UI only, no backend), theme (dark is fixed for MVP), export/delete data placeholders. Mostly UI. Files: app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx

Step 12 — Wire up auth redirect in dashboard layout: if no auth cookie present on server, redirect('/login'). If cookie present but invalid, redirect('/login'). Ensure DEMO_ANALYSIS is seeded and returned for the demo user so dashboard always has data to show. Update lib/store.ts initialization to ensure demo data is available immediately. Files: app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx, lib/store.ts

Step 13 — Add a top-level error boundary at app/error.tsx (must be 'use client') and a loading state at app/loading.tsx. Add app/not-found.tsx for 404. Also add app/(dashboard)/error.tsx for dashboard-level errors. Files: app/error.tsx, app/loading.tsx, app/not-found.tsx, app/(dashboard)/error.tsx

Step 14 — Final integration: ensure all pages import from the correct paths (@/components, @/lib, @/types, @/hooks). Remove the placeholder app/page.tsx that may still be at root if FEAT-004 replaced it. Run a final TypeScript check. Verify that: (a) the demo user can log in; (b) DEMO_ANALYSIS is served at GET /api/analysis/demo-analysis-id; (c) dashboard page renders with demo data; (d) all 6 analysis tabs render without errors. Files: all previously created files as needed for final fixups
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard layout redirects to /login if no auth cookie
Dashboard page renders 4 stats cards with demo data
Resume upload page accepts files and shows parsed preview
Analyze page submits job description and shows loading animation
Analysis [id] page renders all 6 tabs without errors
ScoreRing SVG displays correct score with color coding
Skills page shows skill bars with gap visualization
Resources page shows filterable resource cards
Progress page renders recharts LineChart with demo data
All pages work with demo@example.com / demo123 login
npm run build passes with zero TypeScript errors
npm run dev starts successfully and serves the app

findings: 1) All 14 steps implemented and build passes with zero TypeScript errors (exit code 0). 2) Dashboard layout uses Next.js 16 async cookies() for server-side auth check; redirects to /login if no valid token. 3) AuthProvider wraps layout children so client hooks work. 4) Dashboard page fetches /api/analysis (GET endpoint added to route.ts) and falls back to DEMO_ANALYSIS for guaranteed demo data. 5) Resume upload page has full state machine (idle→uploading→uploaded→editing) using useResume hook. 6) Analyze page uses useSearchParams + useAnalysis.runAnalysis with LoadingState animation during processing. 7) Analysis [id] page uses useParams() (synchronous in client components per Next.js 16 client component rules). 8) All 6 tabs render: Overview, ATS Report, Skill Gaps, Content, Improvements, Resources. 9) Skills, Resources, Roadmap, Progress pages all fetch from /api/analysis with DEMO_ANALYSIS fallback. 10) Progress page renders recharts LineChart via ProgressChart component with multi-line score tracking. 11) Profile page uses react-hook-form + zod, calls PUT /api/profile. 12) Settings page is UI-only with toggle rows for notification preferences. 13) app/error.tsx, app/loading.tsx, app/not-found.tsx, and app/(dashboard)/error.tsx all created. 14) GET /api/analysis endpoint added to return user analyses list. 15) SkillBar uses correct props (skillName + current). 16) RecommendedActions receives ActionItem[] not string[]. 17) npm run build: 25 routes compiled, TypeScript check passes, static + dynamic pages generated.
